correctness.rationale: Under the actual Definition 3.8, the two fixed-point equations for a nonzero element force gh to be the idempotent at that element's cell, unless gh is the global identity. Thus all nonglobal domains are either {0} or {0} plus one maximal subgroup. For cells e=(i,lambda), f=(k,nu) with entries p,q, the pair g=(i,a,nu), h=(k,q^-1 a^-1 p^-1,lambda) has gh=e_id and hg=f_id. In the normalized group coordinates the bridge acts by x ↦ (aq)^-1 x(aq), and all such labels occur, with equality precisely modulo the center. A single adjoined identity in a conjugator pair gives at most a local identity; the pair (1,1) gives the global one. Composing bridges takes products of right-action labels at matching cells and collapses to the identity on {0} at mismatches. This proves the classification without finiteness assumptions. Regularity makes the singleton-cell case a one-by-one matrix, so no extra identity is needed there. In the example the row idempotent counts are {2,2} and {3,1}, and both 18-element counts are 4^2+2.
